result.regime_read: The broad market backdrop over the next three months is not clear from the evidence. Two threads are visible: hot inflation and rising Treasury yields are pressuring debt-funded AI and data-center names, while a vaccine-sector bid and the December 2026 start of the NIH cancer-vaccine programme are lifting vaccine shares.
result.portfolio_posture: Keep position sizes small and let the two pending reports, JetBlue on 27 October 2026 and Moderna on 6 November 2026, decide direction before adding risk.

candidates.setup: JetBlue's shares keep falling because losses widen even as revenue grows, and the third-quarter report on 27 October 2026 is the next hard test.
candidates.hypothesis: Costs are rising faster than the money JetBlue collects per seat, so cash keeps leaving the business and the shares stay under pressure over the next three months.
evidence: Revenue rose about 14.5% from a year earlier to $2.697bn in the quarter ended 30 June 2026, but the net loss widened to $247m from $74m, which shows costs outrunning pricing.
Free cash flow was -$318m in that quarter and has been negative in every quarter shown since late 2024, so the airline keeps funding itself from outside.
S&P lowered JetBlue's credit rating to CCC+ on 8 June 2026, and in the week to 14 October 2026 Susquehanna cut its target to $4 and Goldman Sachs cut to $3.50 with a Sell rating.
candidates.invalidation: The 27 October 2026 report shows a narrower loss with unit revenue growing faster than unit cost, or a credit rater lifts the outlook.
tail_risks: A fall in fuel prices or capacity cuts that slow cost growth faster than expected.
A new share issue or expensive borrowing that management presents as fully funded, which can lift the shares even as it dilutes holders.
An industry-wide fare or demand recovery that lifts all airlines regardless of JetBlue's own progress.
evidence_limits: Unit revenue against unit cost in the 27 October 2026 report, because that single comparison decides whether the loss narrows or widens.
Liquidity and the debt maturing over the next twelve months, because they set how long the cash burn can continue without new funding.
The fuel hedge position and the current share count, because they fix the cost base and the dilution math.

candidates.setup: Moderna has risen about 297% over three months on a cancer-vaccine trial win, and its seasonally strongest quarter is reported on 6 November 2026.
candidates.hypothesis: Moderna enters its strongest selling season with three approved vaccines, a Phase 3 cancer-vaccine win and a newly funded balance sheet, so recent gains can hold through the 6 November 2026 report.
evidence: On 19 August 2026 the Phase 3 INTerpath-001 trial of intismeran autogene with KEYTRUDA met its recurrence-free and distant-metastasis-free survival goals in resected high-risk melanoma, which is the operating fact behind the rally.
mFLUSIVA won FDA approval on 5 August 2026, giving a third approved product in the fall and winter selling window.
An upsized convertible offering in August 2026 raised about $2.96bn net, so the company has no near-term funding need.
candidates.invalidation: Third-quarter revenue comes in far below the roughly $1bn booked in the same quarter of 2025, or the company cuts its outlook.
tail_risks: A $950m litigation payment and a shrinking COVID vaccine franchise keep consuming cash.
A regulatory delay or negative review for the melanoma vaccine, which is the reason investors bought the move.
Momentum unwinds quickly once index-fund buying ends, in a stock already above an overbought reading.
evidence_limits: Whether Merck has filed for approval of intismeran autogene, because a filing date sets when oncology revenue can begin.
The interest rate, maturity and conversion price of the August 2026 convertible notes, because they set the future dilution.
Whether the NIH cancer-vaccine programme, due to start in December 2026, reaches Moderna specifically.

candidates.setup: Core Scientific fell about 35% over three months as borrowing costs rose for data-center builders, and it must still raise outside money to finish its build-out.
candidates.hypothesis: Core Scientific funds its data-center build with debt and equity while the build consumes cash, so rising financing costs keep pressure on the shares over the next three months.
evidence: Free cash flow was -$1.02bn in the quarter ended 30 June 2026, mostly capital spending, and liabilities of $7.68bn exceeded assets of $5.26bn, leaving stockholders' equity at -$2.42bn.
Revenue more than doubled to $164.2m with operating income of $20.7m in the same quarter, so the strain comes from funding the build, not from the operating business.
The AMD capacity partnership announced on 28 July 2026 covers 500+ MW from 2027, but no signed lease terms, rents or start dates are public, so the bull case rests on contracts not yet shown.
candidates.invalidation: Announcements turn into signed leases with named counterparties, disclosed rents and start dates that beat the cost of the new debt, or financing costs fall sharply.
tail_risks: A sharp fall in Treasury yields or a turn in AI-financing sentiment that re-rates the whole data-center group upward.
New equity or debt raised on terms the market reads as fully funding the build-out.
Conditional Texas power approvals become firm approvals and remove a build-out obstacle.
evidence_limits: Signed lease terms, including counterparty, rent, term and start date, for the AMD-backed and other pipeline capacity, because they decide whether the build earns more than its debt cost.
Third-quarter 2026 results, because they show whether the cash outflow is still growing.
The CoreWeave deal termination date, because it frames how investors read Core Scientific's strategic options.

candidates.setup: Strive holds 32,773 bitcoin after buying 3,311 coins for about $280m in early October 2026, and it plans a $500m preferred-share sale.
candidates.hypothesis: Strive adds bitcoin without issuing common shares, so the bitcoin behind each share rises only if bitcoin's return beats the 13-15% dividends paid to preferred holders.
evidence: Strive bought 3,311 bitcoin for about $280m, at roughly $84,500 each, between 5 and 9 October 2026, lifting holdings to 32,773 coins.

A $500m sale of 5 million SATS preferred shares at $100 each, paying 15%, is announced but not completed, and the existing SATA class pays about 13%, so roughly $75m a year in fixed dividends ranks ahead of the common stock.
In one August 2026 window, bitcoin holdings grew 5.5% while bitcoin per diluted share grew only 1.3%, so purchases did not reach common holders one for one.
candidates.invalidation: Bitcoin per share stops rising, the preferred-share sale is cut or priced on worse terms, or the common stock trades below the value of the bitcoin behind it.
tail_risks: A fall in the bitcoin price, because Strive reports its coins at market value and the common stock carries the preferred dividends.
Preferred holders rank ahead of common holders for payouts, so weak bitcoin returns send the leftover value to them.
Any common-share sales to fund purchases would thin the bitcoin behind each share.
evidence_limits: The current count of common shares outstanding, because bitcoin per share against the share price decides whether the stock is cheap or expensive.
The source of the money used for the October purchases, because borrowing or new preferred stock changes the risk the common shares carry.
The pending SATS sale outcome, including size and dividend terms, because it sets how much more bitcoin can be bought.

data_gaps: The path of inflation and interest rates over the next three months, which drives both the data-center short and the strength of the vaccine bid.
Whether the NIH personalised cancer-vaccine programme, due to start in December 2026, names specific companies.
The bitcoin price direction, because one watchlist name holds bitcoin and reports it at market value.
